wins.text: Full-year net income of $50B, EPS of $16.23, revenue of $162B, and ROTCE of 21% — all record results for the firm
IB fees up 13% YoY in Q4; ranked #1 in IB wallet share at 8.8% for the full year
AWM record client asset net inflows of $489B for the year; AUM of $3.4T and client assets of $5T both up 24% YoY
Auto originations of $9.9B, up 32% YoY with market share gains while retaining strong margins
CET1 ratio improved to 15%, up 70 bps QoQ, providing significant capital buffer above regulatory requirements

risks.text: $2.9B FDIC special assessment and $743M net investment securities losses weighed on Q4 results, reducing reported EPS to $3.04
2024 NII ex-Markets guided to ~$88B, implying meaningful sequential quarterly declines from the $94B Q4 annualized run rate as rates normalize
Card net charge-offs up $791M YoY in Q4 due to continued normalization; net reserve build of $538M driven by card loan growth
CRE reserve build of $142M in Commercial Bank driven by deterioration in commercial real estate valuation outlook; C&I loan demand muted with lower revolver utilization
2024 adjusted expenses guided to ~$90B, up ~$7B YoY, driven by compensation, branch expansion, technology, and marketing investments with uncertain near-term ROI visibility

guidance_items.detail: 2024 NII ex-Markets guided to ~$88B vs. Q4 annualized run rate of ~$94B, implying meaningful sequential quarterly declines; total NII ~$90B
ROTCE expected to normalize toward through-the-cycle target of ~17%, down from 21% in 2023, as NII tailwinds dissipate
Card net charge-off rate expected to remain below 3.5% in 2024, consistent with prior Investor Day guidance
2024 adjusted expenses guided to ~$90B, up ~$7B YoY, driven by business growth, technology, and compensation investments
Buyback pace to remain modest at ~$2B net per quarter pending Basel III end-game rule finalization and SCB clarity

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Private credit competitive threat and JPM's strategic response to direct lending and asset-backed finance share shift
Sensitivity of NII outlook to varying number of Fed rate cuts (e.g., 2 vs. 4 vs. 6 cuts)
QT impact on system-wide deposit balances and whether it has been less disruptive than expected
